lean.statement: theorem exists_functorial_bounded_injective_resolution_of_object_resolution {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] (E : C ⥤ CochainComplex C ℕ) (ε : (CochainComplex.single₀ C) ⟶ E) (hε : ∀ A : C, QuasiIso (ε.app A)) (hEzero : ∀ (A B : C), E.map (0 : A ⟶ B) = 0) (hEobjzero : IsZero (E.obj (0 : C))) (hE : ∀ (A : C) (n : ℕ), Injective ((E.obj A).X n)) : ∃ (I : Plus C ⥤ Plus C) (α : Plus.ι C ⟶ I ⋙ Plus.ι C), (∀ K : Plus C, QuasiIso (α.app K)) ∧ (∀ (K : Plus C) (n : ℤ), Injective (((I.obj K).obj).X n)) ∧ (∀ (K : Plus C) (a : ℤ), K.obj.IsStrictlyGE a → (I.obj K).obj.IsStrictlyGE a)

title: Totalization of functorial object injective resolutions
statement: Given a functor E : C ⥤ CochainComplex C ℕ with a natural quasi-isomorphic augmentation from single₀ C, with E mapping zero morphisms to zero, E.obj 0 a zero complex, and with injective terms, there exist a functor I : Plus C ⥤ Plus C and a natural quasi-isomorphism Plus.ι C ⟶ I ⋙ Plus.ι C whose terms are injective and which preserves every strict lower bound.

proof.text: Apply E degreewise to a bounded-below integer-indexed complex to form the bicomplex with resolution degree nonnegative and complex degree integer. Use finite biproducts on each diagonal and the standard signed total differential to define I functorially. The first-quadrant column augmentation theorem gives a quasi-isomorphism after choosing a lower bound only for verification; finite biproducts of injectives and the zero terms below the bound give the remaining assertions uniformly in the bound.
